page: Amazon Web Services m5d.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is delivered by Intel Xeon 8175M processors operating at 3.1 GHz, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU feature set includes AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction extensions. System memory comprises 192 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include discrete GPUs and provides a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps.

Storage capability is anchored by 1800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-throughput I/O operations without depending solely on network-attached block storage. Benchmark data reflects moderate multi-core throughput alongside lower single-core execution speed. Single-threaded metrics, including 1148.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1383.39 on stress-ng, place per-core throughput in the lower quartile. In contrast, parallel benchmarks place within the median range, registering 40468.64 on stress-ng multi-core, 10551.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 34393.15 on PassMark CPU. Memory bandwidth achieves 107.02 GB/s read and 46.35 GB/s write on large blocks, while application tests yield 38.6 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 27.71 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure and efficiency standpoint, m5d.12xlarge offers dense aggregate compute and memory resources combined with integrated high-speed local disk capacity. Although single-thread instruction performance is constrained relative to newer processor architectures, the 48-vCPU configuration handles highly parallelized tasks effectively. The included NVMe storage avoids network storage egress and latency for transient data. The instance is suited for relational database engines requiring fast temporary tables, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
